text: $105 mln packaging plant opens in Vietnam central
A&C International Packaging Joint Stock Company o n November 6 held the inauguration ceremony for Phase 1 of its plant at Quan Ngang Industrial Park in Gio Linh Commune, central Quang Tri Province.
The project spans nearly 10 hectares and is developed in two phases.
Phase 1 carries an investment of nearly VND2.3 trillion ($90.5 million), while Phase 2 represents nearly VND400 billion ($15.7 million).
Upon full completion, the facility will boast a total designed capacity of 1 billion aluminum cans per year, with Phase 1 delivering 700 million units and Phase 2 adding 300 million units.
As a major industrial project in Quan Ngang Industrial Park, the plant aims to establish an aluminum packaging manufacturing hub serving both domestic and export markets.
The investment aligns with Camel Group's long-term strategy to complete its supply chain and secure an active source of aluminum packaging production.

According to Mr. Le Quang Thinh, Member of the Board of Directors and representative of A&C International Packaging Joint Stock Company, the enterprise invested in a fully automated, closed-loop production line imported from the United States and European countries.
Alongside expanding capacity, the plant focuses on technical innovation, material conservation, and developing highly recyclable aluminum packaging to meet escalating market demands.
Notably, the project commenced operations six months ahead of schedule.
According to the Q3/2026 report, the investor disbursed over VND1.78 trillion ($70 million), accounting for approximately 67 percent of the total registered capital.
Beyond boosting manufacturing capacity for the packaging industry, the facility creates job opportunities for the local workforce.
Ahead of the inauguration, the company hired 100 workers, primarily local residents.
As production expands, the plant plans to recruit hundreds more employees to support operations.

Speaking at the ceremony, Mr. Le Duc Tien, Vice Chairman of the Quang Tri Provincial People ' s Committee, emphasized that the true value of an investment project lies not only in registered capital but also in manufacturing capacity, product off-take, job creation, and long-term societal contributions.
He urged the enterprise to complete remaining items and implement Phase 2 as planned, while prioritizing occupational safety, environmental protection, workforce training, and employee welfare.
Local government departments were tasked with resolving operational hurdles and improving industrial park infrastructure to facilitate stable production and market expansion for the business.
